findings.title: Insecure Cryptographic Algorithms in HTTP Digest Authentication
findings.description: The code change adds `usedforsecurity=False` to MD5 and SHA-1 hash functions used in HTTP Digest authentication. MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken and unsuitable for security purposes. Using `usedforsecurity=False` does not mitigate the underlying weakness; it merely suppresses deprecation warnings. HTTP Digest authentication using MD5 or SHA-1 algorithms is insecure and should be avoided in favor of stronger algorithms like SHA-256.
findings.suggestion: Enforce the use of SHA-256 or stronger algorithms for HTTP Digest authentication. Deprecate or disable MD5 and SHA-1 support. Update clients and servers to use `algorithm=SHA-256` or higher. If MD5/SHA-1 must be retained for legacy compatibility, document the risk and plan a migration path to stronger algorithms.
